Cotini.subject: Environment & Ecology
Cotini.question: The _____ was Ancient Celtic people of the Carpathians.
Cotini.fact: The Cotini (also Gotini) were an ancient Celtic people of the northern part of the Carpathian basin, in the mountainous regions of present-day Slovakia. After the Marcomannic Wars part of the people was resettled within Pannonia, where their descendants are attested as cives Cotini.

Cotini.subject: Environment & Ecology
Cotini.question: They are recorded by _____, Ptolemy and Cassius Dio, and in Latin inscriptions, between the reign of Augustus and the middle of the 3rd century AD
Cotini.fact: They are recorded by Tacitus, Ptolemy and Cassius Dio, and in Latin inscriptions, between the reign of Augustus and the middle of the 3rd century AD.

Cotini.subject: Environment & Ecology
Cotini.question: Subject to the Quadi and noted as ironworkers, they were a _____-speaking people, unlike their neighbours the Osi
Cotini.fact: The Cotini (also Gotini) were an ancient Celtic people of the northern part of the Carpathian basin, in the mountainous regions of present-day Slovakia. Subject to the Quadi and noted as ironworkers, they were a Celtic-speaking people, unlike their neighbours the Osi.

Cotini.subject: Environment & Ecology
Cotini.question: If of _____ origin, the name has been derived from a stem *cot(t)o- and explained as 'the old ones', a sense compared with that of the Senones (from *seno-, 'old')
Cotini.fact: Subject to the Quadi and noted as ironworkers, they were a Celtic-speaking people, unlike their neighbours the Osi. If of Celtic origin, the name has been derived from a stem *cot(t)o- and explained as 'the old ones', a sense compared with that of the Senones (from *seno-, 'old').

Cotini.subject: Environment & Ecology
Cotini.question: A _____ interpretation is generally preferred, on the strength of Tacitus's statement about the people's language
Cotini.fact: Subject to the Quadi and noted as ironworkers, they were a Celtic-speaking people, unlike their neighbours the Osi. If of Celtic origin, the name has been derived from a stem *cot(t)o- and explained as 'the old ones', a sense compared with that of the Senones (from *seno-, 'old').

Cotini.subject: Environment & Ecology
Cotini.question: Two non-_____ interpretations have also been advanced
Cotini.fact: If of Celtic origin, the name has been derived from a stem *cot(t)o- and explained as 'the old ones', a sense compared with that of the Senones (from *seno-, 'old'). A Celtic interpretation is generally preferred, on the strength of Tacitus's statement about the people's language.

Cotini.subject: Environment & Ecology
Cotini.question: Peter Anreiter traces the name instead to a _____ kōtiā ('dwelling, hut'), from Proto-Indo-European *kōt-
Cotini.fact: Peter Anreiter traces the name instead to a Pannonian kōtiā ('dwelling, hut'), from Proto-Indo-European *kōt-.

Cotini.subject: Environment & Ecology
Cotini.question: A _____ origin, suggested by Zsolt Visy, has been rejected as resting on probably unrelated forms, while the variant reading got(h)ini has prompted attempts to connect the name with Germanic
Cotini.fact: A Dacian origin, suggested by Zsolt Visy, has been rejected as resting on probably unrelated forms, while the variant reading got(h)ini has prompted attempts to connect the name with Germanic.

Cotini.subject: Environment & Ecology
Cotini.question: An older view placing them, with other _____ groups, in the territory of modern Poland is no longer accepted, although small enclaves there have been discussed
Cotini.fact: The principal evidence for the Celtic character of the Cotini is the statement of Tacitus that they spoke Gallica lingua (Celtic), in contrast to the Pannonica of the neighbouring Osi. An older view placing them, with other Celtic groups, in the territory of modern Poland is no longer accepted, although small enclaves there have been discussed.

Cotini.subject: Environment & Ecology
Cotini.question: They were subject to the Quadi, and paid tribute also to the _____
Cotini.fact: They were subject to the Quadi, and paid tribute also to the Sarmatians.

Cotini.subject: Environment & Ecology
Cotini.question: Together with the Osi, the _____, the Anarti and the Teurisci they have been regarded as forming a single Celtic group of the northern Carpathian region
Cotini.fact: Together with the Osi, the Eravisci, the Anarti and the Teurisci they have been regarded as forming a single Celtic group of the northern Carpathian region.

Cotini.subject: Environment & Ecology
Cotini.question: The community later settled within _____ cannot be located precisely, the most likely area being south of Lake Pelso, between the Azali and the Iasi
Cotini.fact: The community later settled within Pannonia cannot be located precisely, the most likely area being south of Lake Pelso, between the Azali and the Iasi.

Cotini.subject: Environment & Ecology
Cotini.question: By the time they were incorporated into the empire most of them bore _____ names
Cotini.fact: The Cotini and Osi, left outside the empire, came under the control of the Quadi and the Sarmatians and were gradually Dacianised, whereas the Eravisci, under Roman rule, retained their Celtic language and culture. By the time they were incorporated into the empire most of them bore Dacian names.

Cotini.subject: Environment & Ecology
Cotini.question: Roman troops under the command of _____ were stationed in their territory in order to attack the Marcomanni to the west
Cotini.fact: Roman troops under the command of Tarrutenius Paternus were stationed in their territory in order to attack the Marcomanni to the west.
